transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hey, yeah, thanks. Um, honestly, the thing that actually scared me into coming in today is that my eating has just been completely all over the place. Like, some days I'll just totally forget meals completely, not a single bite. And then other nights, I'm up past midnight just tearing through takeout and whatever snacks I can get my hands on. 

It's weird because, you know, I do wholesale sales, so I'm in my car a lot, driving to different manufacturing plants and stuff. You'd think I'd just be hitting drive-thrus all the time. Actually, speaking of driving, I just had to get my transmission fixed because it was making this awful grinding noise every time I shifted into third gear. The mechanic tried to overcharge me by like four hundred bucks. Can you believe that? Good thing I know a little bit about cars from back in high school. I used to have this old Ford, and my buddy and I were always messing around under the hood. He actually just moved to Texas, which is crazy because... wait, sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, right. Yeah, so my appetite is just really messed up right now.
Have you lost any weight recently?

Weight? I mean, I don't even own a scale, so I'm not totally sure. But like I was just saying, my eating is just completely unpredictable right now. Since I'm either going the whole day without a single bite or binging on late-night takeout until 2 AM, my weight is probably just as confused as I am. 

I did notice my favorite work pants are fitting kinda weird, though. Actually, I think I might have just ruined them in the wash. I have to use this really sketchy laundromat down on 4th street because the dryer in my apartment building has been broken for like a month. My landlord is so cheap, he keeps saying he’s gonna fix it, but I literally saw him at the grocery store the other night when I was doing one of my midnight junk food runs, and he was buying like, a dozen pineapples. Who even needs that many pineapples? Unless he's throwing some kind of massive luau or making a ton of fruit salad or something. It's just weird. But yeah, I haven't stepped on a scale to check the number, I just know my appetite is bouncing back and forth to extremes.
Do you feel guilty after eating a lot of food in one sitting?

Guilty? Um... I don't know if guilt is the right word. It's more like... I just feel really full and kind of gross, you know? Like I just shoved way too much in the tank. Speaking of tanks, gas prices right now are absolutely insane. I filled up my car yesterday and it was almost sixty bucks. Sixty! And I have to drive so much for work, hitting all those manufacturing plants, it's really eating into my commission. My boss says we might get a gas allowance next quarter, but he's been saying that since last year. He's one of those guys who wears a suit but always has mustard on his tie, you know the type? Just completely disorganized. I saw his desk once and it was just mountains of paper. I don't know how he finds anything. But, um, what were we talking about? Oh, right, the food. Yeah, no, not really guilty, just... physically uncomfortable, I guess.
Do you usually eat more when you're stressed or anxious?

Stressed? I mean, maybe a little? But honestly, like I was saying before, the main thing that really scared me into coming in today is just how my eating is completely all over the place, stress or no stress. It's like, some days I just totally forget to eat completely, not a single bite all day. And then other nights, I'm just tearing through takeout and snacks way past midnight. 

It's actually kind of like how my dog eats, now that I think about it. I have this golden retriever mix, Buster, and he is just the weirdest eater. Sometimes he'll just stare at his bowl all day, completely ignoring it, even if I put the expensive wet food in there. And then other times, I'll catch him trying to break into the pantry to get to his treats. He actually figured out how to open the sliding door with his nose, which is pretty smart for a dog who regularly gets stuck behind the couch. I had to put a baby lock on the pantry door, which is super annoying when I'm doing my own midnight snack raids because I always forget it's there and just yank on the handle. I almost pulled the whole door off the hinges last week. But yeah, stress... I don't know if that's the trigger, it's just really erratic right now.
Do you think your mood has anything to do with whether you eat a lot or hardly at all on a given day?

My mood? I mean, maybe? But honestly, like I've been saying, the whole reason I even made this appointment—the thing that really freaked me out and made me come in—is just that my eating is completely all over the place right now. It's just so erratic. Like I said, some days I'll go the entire day and completely forget to eat a single meal, and then other nights I'm just tearing through takeout boxes and snacks way past midnight. 

It's actually kind of like how the weather has been lately, you know? Like, one day it's freezing and I have to wear my heavy winter coat, and the next day I'm sweating in a t-shirt. I had to scrape ice off my windshield on Tuesday, and by Thursday I had the AC blasting in my car on the way to a client meeting. And my car's AC isn't even that great, it makes this weird rattling noise whenever I turn it past the second notch. I took it to the mechanic last month and he said it was a loose fan belt or something, but he wanted to charge me like three hundred dollars just to look at it. Three hundred dollars! I told him I'd just live with the rattling. It kind of sounds like a snare drum if you listen to it long enough. I used to play the snare drum in middle school band, actually. We played at the Thanksgiving parade one year and it rained the whole time. My uniform smelled like wet dog for a week. But anyway, yeah, my eating is just totally unpredictable right now, regardless of my mood.
Have you noticed any changes in your interest in activities you usually enjoy?

Activities I usually enjoy? Yeah, I mean... I used to do a lot of stuff. Like, I used to play soccer on the weekends with this rec league, and I loved cooking dinner for my girlfriend, going to check out these little art galleries downtown, even just helping out the newer sales guys at work. But lately, I just... I can't make myself care about any of it. It's just too much effort. 

Speaking of the newer sales guys, we just hired this kid, Kevin. He's fresh out of high school, just like I was when I started, but man, he is clueless. He wore a tuxedo to our quarterly regional meeting. A tuxedo! I mean, it's a paper products manufacturing company, not the Oscars. The boss didn't even know what to say, he just stared at him for like a solid minute before asking him if he was going to prom later. Kevin got so red, I actually felt kind of bad for him. I remember my first big meeting, I spilled coffee all over my presentation folders. The ink ran everywhere, it looked like a tie-dye project. But anyway, yeah, I just haven't had the energy or interest to do much of anything I used to like.
Is your lack of interest in doing things you used to enjoy more because you're tired or because you just don't feel like doing them anymore?

It's... I think it's because I'm just so tired. Like, physically drained. Even when I do try to just lie down and rest for hours, my body still feels completely spent the next day. Like, just carrying my sample cases into a client meeting takes way more out of me than it should. 

And those sample cases are heavy, man. They're these big, bulky black plastic things with all these different grades of paperboard inside. My boss, Mr. Henderson, he insists we bring the full physical samples to every single pitch, even though everyone just looks at the digital specs on their iPads anyway. Mr. Henderson is really old school like that. He still uses a Rolodex. I didn't even know what a Rolodex was until I started working there, I thought it was some kind of fancy watch. He's got this massive one on his desk that spins around, and he's always licking his thumb to flip through the little cards. It's kind of gross, honestly, especially during flu season. Last year, half the office got sick because he refused to stay home when he had a fever. He just sat there coughing all over the client files. But yeah, the fatigue is just... it's really dragging me down right now.
Do you think your eating changes when you're feeling sad or upset?

I mean, like I was saying before, I really don't know if feeling sad is what's causing it. I just know that my eating being so all over the place is the main thing that scared me into actually coming in here to see you. It's just completely extreme—like forgetting to eat anything all day, and then tearing through a mountain of takeout and snacks well past midnight. 

Actually, speaking of takeout, I've been ordering way too much from this Chinese place near my apartment lately. They always give you those little fortune cookies, right? Well, the last one I opened didn't even have a fortune in it. It was just an empty cookie. My buddy Mike said I should call and complain, but Mike complains about literally everything. He sent a steak back three times at a restaurant once because he said it wasn't "medium-rare enough." Three times! The waiter looked like he wanted to punch him. I used to wait tables back in high school before I got into the paper business, and let me tell you, you do not want to make the kitchen staff mad. I saw a line cook drop a burger patty on the floor, pick it up, and throw it right back on the grill like nothing happened. I didn't say anything because the guy was like six-foot-four and had a neck tattoo of a scorpion. But anyway, yeah, I'm not really sure if I'm upset when the eating stuff happens, it just feels totally random.

Like I said, I really don't know if feeling sad is what's causing it. I just know that my eating being so all over the place is the main thing that scared me into actually coming in here to see you. It's just completely extreme—like forgetting to eat anything all day, and then tearing through a mountain of takeout and snacks well past midnight. 

Actually, speaking of takeout, I've been ordering way too much from this Chinese place near my apartment lately. They always give you those little fortune cookies, right? Well, the last one I opened didn't even have a fortune in it. It was just an empty cookie. My buddy Mike said I should call and complain, but Mike complains about literally everything. He sent a steak back three times at a restaurant once because he said it wasn't "medium-rare enough." Three times! The waiter looked like he wanted to punch him. I used to wait tables back in high school before I got into the paper business, and let me tell you, you do not want to make the kitchen staff mad. I saw a line cook drop a burger patty on the floor, pick it up, and throw it right back on the grill like nothing happened. I didn't say anything because the guy was like six-foot-four and had a neck tattoo of a scorpion. But anyway, yeah, I'm not really sure if I'm upset when the eating stuff happens, it just feels totally random.
Do you think your eating changes are related to how you're feeling emotionally?

Doc, I feel like we're going in circles here. Like I keep saying, I really don't know if my emotions have anything to do with it. I just know that my eating being so all over the place is honestly the main thing that scared me into coming in here to see you. It's just totally extreme—like some days I'll completely forget to have a single meal, and then other nights I'm up past midnight just tearing through takeout and whatever snacks I can find. 

Speaking of snacks, I actually bought this massive box of those spicy nacho chips from the wholesale club last week. You know the ones where the bag is like the size of a pillow? I have this membership card I share with my sister. Technically you're not supposed to share them, they actually check your picture at the door now. This one greeter, this older lady with thick glasses, she squinted at my card for like two solid minutes because my sister has long blonde hair and I obviously don't. I had to talk my way out of it and say it was a joint family account. They take that stuff way too seriously, like they're guarding Fort Knox or something. But anyway... what were we talking about? Oh, right, emotions. Yeah, I don't really notice a connection there.
Do you ever feel like your emotions, such as sadness or anxiety, influence when you eat or how much you eat?

Look, doctor, I don't mean to be difficult, but I really feel like I've answered this already. I honestly don't know if being sad or anxious is what's doing it. I just know that my eating being so completely all over the place is the main thing that actually scared me into making this appointment. It's just extreme—like, I'll go all day and totally forget to eat a single thing, and then I'll be up at 2 AM just tearing through a mountain of takeout and whatever snacks are in the pantry. 

Which reminds me, I actually need to clean out my pantry. I found a can of soup the other day that expired in 2019. Can you believe that? 2019! That was before I even moved into this apartment. I must have packed it in a box and just brought it with me. Moving is the absolute worst. I hired these movers last time, and they charged me by the hour, right? But they took so many breaks. I caught one of them just sitting in the back of the truck eating a sandwich for like twenty minutes. And it wasn't even a good sandwich, it looked like one of those pre-packaged gas station ones. I don't know how people eat those, they always taste like cardboard and regret. But yeah, anyway, the eating thing... I don't really see a connection to my mood. It just happens.
Have you experienced any significant weight loss recently?

Look, doc, like I've been saying this whole time, I don't know my exact weight because I don't even own a scale. I actually threw mine out because it was scratching up the floor in my bathroom. It's that cheap peel-and-stick stuff that landlords try to pass off as "luxury vinyl." I work in wholesale, right? I sell supplies to contractors all day, so I know exactly what that flooring costs per square foot. It's literally pennies. My landlord, this guy Gary, tried to tell me it was imported from Italy. Italy! I just laughed in his face. Gary drives this beat-up old sedan that always smells like wet dog, so I don't think he knows much about Italian imports. He's always trying to cut corners. 

But anyway, weight loss... I really couldn't tell you a number. All I know is what I've been trying to explain to you: the main thing that freaked me out enough to actually make this appointment is just how completely chaotic my eating is right now. Like, going the whole entire day and just forgetting to eat a single bite, and then being up way past midnight to absolutely demolish a mountain of takeout and snacks. My appetite is just completely all over the place.
Do you notice any pattern between your emotions and when these extreme eating episodes happen?

Doc, I swear we're going in circles. I don't mean to be rude, but I feel like you've asked me this three times now. I don't notice any pattern with my emotions. I really don't. Like I keep saying, the only thing I know for sure—the whole reason I even walked into this clinic—is that my eating is just totally chaotic right now. Some days I won't eat a single thing, I just completely forget, and then other nights I'm up at 2 AM absolutely destroying a pile of takeout and snacks. 

Speaking of takeout, I ordered from this new Thai place down the street the other night. They said it would be 45 minutes, but it took an hour and a half. And when the guy finally showed up, he couldn't figure out the buzzer system for my building. It's not that complicated, you just press the unit number and the green button. But he was pressing the red button, which calls the super. So my super, Gary—the guy with the cheap floors—gets woken up at 1:30 in the morning and he's yelling at the delivery guy through the intercom. I had to run downstairs in my socks to get my food before Gary called the cops. And by the time I got back upstairs, the Pad Thai was cold. I still ate it, obviously, because I was starving, but cold noodles just aren't the same. Have you ever tried to microwave Pad Thai? It gets all gummy. But yeah, no, I don't see any emotional pattern with the eating. It's just all over the place.
Do you think your eating changes are directly triggered by how you're feeling at a particular moment?

Doc, are you messing with me right now? Is this like a trick question or some kind of psychological test to see if I lose my temper? Because I feel like I literally just answered this exact same thing. I don't know how else to explain it to you. I don't know about my feelings or triggers at any particular moment. Honestly, the thing that scared me into coming in is just that my eating has been all over the place, like some days I forget meals completely and other nights I'm tearing through takeout and snacks after midnight. 

Like last night, I was eating these jalapeño chips I got from the bodega on my corner. The guy who runs it, Sammy, he always tries to overcharge me. Which is insulting, because I work in wholesale, right? I sell supplies to contractors. I know exactly how retail markup works. I see the invoices for the drywall and the power tools we sell, so you can't tell me a standard bag of chips costs six bucks. I told Sammy, "Look man, I know your profit margins." And he just suddenly pretended he didn't understand English, which is hilarious because we were literally just arguing about the Mets five minutes before that. The Mets are an absolute disaster this year, by the way. My buddy Dave bet a hundred bucks on them last week and lost it all. I told him he might as well just set his cash on fire or use it as wall insulation. Insulation is getting really expensive actually, supply chain issues and all that, the fiberglass guys are backed up for months. 

But yeah, no... I don't think my feelings are triggering it. Like I keep saying, it's just completely random.
Are your eating habits interfering with your work or daily activities in any way?

Yeah, I mean... I guess so. I'm still showing up to the office every day, but honestly, work and home both just feel like they're completely slipping out of my control right now. Like, my manager actually started pulling me off some of my accounts because I'm making mistakes I normally wouldn't make. 

He took me off the Miller account. Miller Construction, they do these huge commercial build-outs, mostly office spaces. And let me tell you, commercial office space is a really weird market right now because half the city is still working from home, so Miller is trying to pivot to residential renovations. Which means they need totally different materials, and I accidentally sent them a massive shipment of acoustic drop-ceiling tiles instead of standard drywall. Who puts a drop ceiling in a house, right? 

So anyway, because of stuff like that, HR actually got involved after this employee-assistance call. The HR lady, Brenda, she sent me this email with all these links to wellness webinars. Have you ever watched a corporate wellness webinar? It's just some guy in a polo shirt telling you to drink more water and do deep breathing while a stock photo of a waterfall plays in the background. Like, Brenda, a waterfall isn't gonna fix the fact that I accidentally ordered three thousand dollars' worth of the wrong silicone caulk last week. Caulk has an expiration date, you know! You can't just leave it sitting in the warehouse forever, it gets all hard in the tubes and then the contractors get pissed when they try to use it and the gun jams up. 

But yeah, I'm still going in. It's just... I don't know, everything is just slipping.
Are your eating habits causing problems in your relationships with family or friends?

I mean... not that I've noticed? I don't think my friends or family really pay attention to what I'm eating, to be honest. 

Like, my mom called me on Sunday while I was eating a bowl of dry cereal at like four in the afternoon, and she didn't even ask about it. She was just going on and on about her neighbor's dog. Her neighbor has this golden retriever that keeps digging up her hydrangeas along the fence line. Which is a shame, because hydrangeas are actually super sensitive to that kind of disruption. They need a really specific soil pH, you know? Like, if the soil is too acidic, the flowers turn blue, and if it's alkaline, they go pink. 

We actually sell this bulk landscaping compound at work that adjusts soil pH, but we mostly sell it to commercial golf courses. You would not believe the insane amount of chemicals a golf course uses just to keep the grass looking perfect. It's thousands of gallons of turf builder and nitrogen a year. I see the purchase orders all the time. I tried to tell my mom she should just buy some lime powder to fix the soil where the dog ruined it, but she just wants to complain to the HOA instead. The HOA in her neighborhood is a total nightmare anyway, they fined a guy last month just because his mailbox was the wrong shade of white. Can you imagine? Fined for a mailbox. 

But, uh... what were we talking about? Oh, right, relationships. Yeah, no, nobody's mad at me about food or my eating habits or anything like that.
Are you finding it harder to do everyday tasks or enjoy hobbies because of your eating habits?

I don't know if it's the eating that's causing it, but... yeah. I just don't really do much of anything right now. 

I used to be pretty active, you know? Like, I used to play soccer on weekends, I'd cook dinner for my girlfriend a lot, we'd go check out these small art galleries in the city... and even at the office, I was always the one helping the newer sales guys figure things out. But lately I just can't make myself care about any of it. Like, at all. 

Take the new guys at work, for example. We just hired this kid, Jason, and he has absolutely zero common sense. The other day he was trying to load a full pallet of quick-set concrete into the back of a customer's standard F-150. A whole pallet! Do you know how heavy quick-set concrete is? It's eighty pounds a bag, fifty bags to a pallet. That's four thousand pounds. You put that in a half-ton pickup and you'll literally snap the rear axle in half. Usually I'd run out there, stop him, explain payload capacities to him so he learns... but I just sat at my desk and watched him do it. I just didn't care. 

If that guy's suspension gets completely destroyed, that's on him. Truck parts are impossible to get right now anyway. My buddy's been waiting on a catalytic converter for his Tacoma for like six months because of the global metal shortages. Platinum and palladium prices are just through the roof right now. People are actually going around with saws and stealing them right out of people's driveways in the middle of the night. It's crazy. 

But, uh... yeah. What were you asking? Oh, hobbies. Yeah, I just don't really care about my weekend stuff or any of that right now.
Are there any daily activities that you're no longer able to do because of your eating habits?

No, I don't think so. Like, there isn't anything I physically can't do because of how I'm eating, if that makes sense. It's not like I'm too weak to walk or anything. 

I still drive to work every day. Though driving has been a total nightmare lately because they're doing all this construction on Interstate 95. They've had the right lane closed for, like, three months now just to repave a two-mile stretch. It's ridiculous. And the asphalt they're using? It's this cheap, high-recycled-content mix that's just going to crack again as soon as the first freeze hits. I know this because we sell the industrial sealants they're supposed to use over the top of it, but the state DOT never approves the budget for the good stuff. They just want the cheapest bid. 

It's just like what happened with that new municipal building downtown. They used this bargain-basement waterproofing membrane on the foundation, and the first time we got heavy rain, the whole basement flooded. Ruined all their servers. Millions of dollars in IT equipment, just gone, because they wanted to save a few grand on materials. I actually tried to warn the contractor, but nobody listens to the sales guy. They think we're just trying to upsell them. But I know my products, you know? I've been doing this since I got out of high school. 

But anyway... yeah. To answer your question, no. My eating habits aren't stopping me from doing my daily stuff.
Are you feeling overwhelmed or unable to cope with your daily life because of your eating habits?

Well, I wouldn't say it's because of my eating habits, but... yeah, things are definitely getting overwhelming. Like, everything just feels like it's slipping out of my control lately. At home, at work... it's just a lot. 

Actually, my manager just started pulling me off some of my bigger accounts. He says I'm making mistakes I normally wouldn't make, which is frustrating because I know these accounts inside and out. Like the Miller Construction account. I've handled them for three years. They order the same bulk adhesives every quarter, but last week I accidentally keyed in the wrong product code and sent them industrial solvent instead. Which, by the way, is a huge hazmat liability to ship by mistake. The freight regulations on solvents are insane right now because of the new EPA guidelines. You have to have special placards on the trucks, the drivers need specific endorsements... it's a whole bureaucratic nightmare. 

And the DOT fines for improper hazmat transport? Astronomical. I was reading this article about a trucking company out of Ohio that went completely bankrupt because one of their drivers didn't secure a load of corrosive chemicals right and it leaked on the highway. The environmental cleanup alone was like two million dollars. They had to scrape up half a mile of asphalt and treat the soil underneath. Soil remediation is actually a massive industry, mostly because of old gas stations with leaking underground storage tanks. People don't realize how many abandoned gas stations are just sitting there, leaching toxins into the groundwater. 

But anyway, yeah, the mistake with the solvent got HR involved, especially after I had that employee-assistance call. So I'm still showing up to work and everything, but... yeah. What were you asking? Overwhelmed? Yeah, it definitely feels like everything is just kind of slipping away from me right now.
Do you think your eating habits might be related to something else going on with your health?

I don't... I don't really know. Like, I haven't noticed any other health stuff going on that would make me eat like this, if that's what you mean. I feel physically fine, mostly. 

Well, except for my allergies. They've been absolutely terrible this year. The pollen count has been off the charts because we had that really mild winter. You know how when it doesn't freeze hard enough, all the trees just dump pollen at once in the spring? It coats everything. My car is basically yellow right now. And you can't just run it through a normal car wash either, because pollen is actually super abrasive. It's basically microscopic spikes. If you just let the spinning brushes hit it, it'll put thousands of tiny micro-scratches in your clear coat. You have to use a foam cannon first to lift the dirt off, then do a two-bucket wash method with grit guards. 

Grit guards are actually a really brilliant invention. It's just a plastic grate that sits at the bottom of the bucket so the dirt falls through and your wash mitt doesn't pick it back up. The guy who invented them made an absolute fortune. It's always the simplest things, right? Like the guy who invented the cardboard sleeve for coffee cups. Millions of dollars for a piece of corrugated cardboard. 

But, uh, health stuff. No, I haven't noticed my eating being related to anything else. Just the allergies, but that's normal for this time of year.
